newsitem.title: UK: Zinc market seen in balance in 1997 - GNI.
newsitem.headline: Zinc market seen in balance in 1997 - GNI.

text.p: The zinc market will be largely balanced next year with little prospect for a significant rise in prices, GNI Research said in an outlook for 1997.

Zinc production is forecast at 7.359 million tonnes in 1997, a rise of 97,000 tonnes from this year. Consumption is seen up 14,000 tonnes at 7.396 million, resulting in a relatively modest supply deficit of 17,000 tonnes.
"If the overall level of stocks is taken into consideration, then there is little reason to expect zinc prices to rise significantly in the coming 12 months," the outlook said.
The forecast increase in production was attributed to modest improvement across the board and expansion by China.
GNI forecast that prices will average between $1,040 and $1,120 for most of next year.

"Prices probably have the ability to reach $1,200 per tonne in a fund and speculative flurry in the latter stages of this year, but unless there is a sharp and noticeable improvement in demand, or further cutbacks in production, there is likely to be little solid support for the market," the report added.

The report discounted market speculation that zinc had a bright price future, sparked by rallies following news that Spanish producer Asturiana de zinc had unwound a position in the and that Anvil Ranges' Faro mine would be temporarily closed.
"The recent excitement in the zinc price has been caused not by a sharp rise in price, but because the three percent rally has been dramatic in comparison to a very dull 1996," it said.

GNI also questioned whether declining LME stocks were being abosorbed by demand or effected by a producer attempt to support prices. Stocks in 1995 declined more than 500,000 tonnes, but GNI's own data showed a deficit of just 57,000 tonnes.
"GNI Research believes that the withdrawal of the metal has only been cosmetic and is still effectively overhanging the market," the report said.
The eventual release of the "invisible stockpile" will lead to an understatement of demand conditions over the period it is being released, GNI said.
